settings.name_in_paper: Multi-bandit contextual linear bandit with hierarchical Gaussian prior (N bandit instances, K arms each)
unmapped: Multi-task: N bandit instances; at each round the instance Z_t is drawn from a categorical distribution p_j, then context x_t drawn i.i.d.
Each arm k in each instance j has its own parameter beta_{k,j} in R^d (disjoint linear model); reward x_t^T beta_{k,j} + Gaussian noise
Hierarchical Gaussian structure beta_{k,j} ~ N(beta_{k0}, Sigma_k) with eigenvalues of Sigma_k^{-1} in [lambda_d, lambda_1]
In the theory the learner knows Sigma_k and sigma (estimated empirically in practice), and the constants c_beta, c_x, lambda_1, lambda_d, N used in alpha_t(delta)
Context bound: d^{-1}||x||^2 <= c_x; parameter norm ||beta_{k,j}|| <= c_beta
settings.definition_quote: We consider a contextual bandit problem with $N$ bandit instances, each associated with $K$ arms. ... $y_{k, j, t} = \mathbf{x}_t^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}_{k,j} + \epsilon_{k,j,t}$ ... $\epsilon_{k,j,t} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_k^2)$ ... $\boldsymbol{\beta}_{k,j} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{k0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k)$

bound.expression_latex: 2\alpha_{n}(\delta) \sqrt{nd K \left[ c_1 \sum_{j=1}^N\log (1 + c_2 n_j)+c_3 \log (1+ c_4 N) \right]} + 2 \sqrt{d c_x}c_{\beta}KNn \delta

symbols.alpha_n: confidence width alpha_n(delta) = 2 sqrt(d m_1 log((m_2 + n c_x)/(m_3 delta))) + N m_4 = O(sqrt(d log(n/delta)))
symbols.S_logn: sum over instances j of log(1 + c_2 n_j)
symbols.n_j: number of arrivals at bandit instance j
symbols.c_1: lambda_d^{-1} d c_x / log(1 + sigma^{-2} lambda_d^{-1} d c_x) = O(d)
symbols.c_3: O(d^2) constant depending on lambda_1, lambda_d, lambda, sigma, c_x

conditions: Assumption 1: ||beta_{k,j}||_2 <= c_beta; d^{-1}||x||_2^2 <= c_x; eigenvalues of Sigma_k^{-1} in [lambda_d, lambda_1] with lambda_d > 0; equal noise variance sigma^2 across arms
Sigma_k and sigma known in the analysis

source.label: regret_bound_ebmUCB
source.quote: For any $\delta > 0$, the overall cumulative regret of \textsc{ebmUCB} is at most $2\alpha_{n}(\delta) \sqrt{nd K \left[ c_1 \sum_{j=1}^N\log (1 + c_2 n_j)+c_3 \log (1+ c_4 N) \right]} + 2 \sqrt{d c_x}c_{\beta}KNn \delta = O\left( d^{3/2}\sqrt{nK\log\frac{n}{\delta} \left(\sum_{j=1}^N \log n_j + d\log N \right) }\right)$

results.notes: Simplified form stated: O(d^{3/2} sqrt(T K log(T/delta) (sum_j log n_j + d log N))). The regret is defined through means (pseudo-regret) against the per-round best arm for the instance and context. The theorem gives no restriction on delta, but the additive term is linear in n*delta. In the proof, P(not xi_t) <= KN delta is obtained from the fixed-t Theorem 2.

bound.expression_latex: 2C \alpha^{\prime}_n(\delta) \sqrt{nd K \left[ c_1 \sum_{j=1}^N\log (1 + c_2 n_j)+c_3 \log (1+ c_4 N)\right]} + 2 \sqrt{d c_x}c_{\beta}KN (n\delta + \pi^2/6)

symbols.C_TS: C = max_{t>=1} 2/|1/(2 sqrt(2 pi e)) - 1/t^2| + 1 (numerical constant)
symbols.alpha_n: confidence width alpha_n(delta) = 2 sqrt(d m_1 log((m_2 + n c_x)/(m_3 delta))) + N m_4 = O(sqrt(d log(n/delta)))
symbols.S_logn: sum over instances j of log(1 + c_2 n_j)
symbols.n_j: number of arrivals at bandit instance j

conditions: Assumption 1: ||beta_{k,j}||_2 <= c_beta; d^{-1}||x||_2^2 <= c_x; eigenvalues of Sigma_k^{-1} in [lambda_d, lambda_1]; equal noise variance sigma^2 across arms
Sigma_k and sigma known in the analysis

source.label: regret_bound_ebmTS
source.quote: For any $\delta > 0$, the overall cumulative regret of \textsc{ebmTS} is at most $R_n \leq 2C \alpha^{\prime}_n(\delta) \sqrt{nd K \left[ c_1 \sum_{j=1}^N\log (1 + c_2 n_j)+c_3 \log (1+ c_4 N)\right]} + 2 \sqrt{d c_x}c_{\beta}KN (n\delta + \pi^2/6) = O\left( d^{2}\sqrt{nK\log\frac{n}{\delta} \log n\left(\sum_{j=1}^N \log n_j + d\log N \right) }\right)$, where ... $\alpha^{\prime}_n(\delta) = ( \gamma_n+1)\alpha_{n}(\delta)$, and $\gamma_n=\sqrt{2d\log (dn^2)}$.

results.notes: Simplified form stated: O(d^2 sqrt(T K log(T/delta) log T (sum_j log n_j + d log N))). gamma_n = sqrt(2d log(d n^2)) is substituted directly into the expression.
